newsitem.title: MEXICO: Interacciones warns on Mexican monetary base rise.
newsitem.headline: Interacciones warns on Mexican monetary base rise.

text.p: Mexico's monetary base has recently risen above levels forecast by Banco de Mexico, which could force it to tighten monetary policy if the trend is not reversed, Interacciones brokerage said.

In a report on Monday entitled Keep an Eye on the Monetary Base, Interacciones chief economist Alonso Cervera said the causes of the increase were still unclear, and that they may have to be explained.

"If the monetary base does not adjust in a sustained way to the levels expected by the central bank, we would expect the adoption of a more restrictive monetary policy or an explanation why the official projections have temporarily not been met," he said.

According to Banco de Mexico data cited by Cervera, the monetary base that measures the amount of notes and coins in circulation has fluctuated above the maximum level projected by Banco de Mexico on most days since March 19.
"Based on statistics available up to last Friday, in 10 of the last 14 working days (71 percent of the time) the central bank's maximum projections of the monetary base have fallen short."

He said the higher-than-expected monetary base could spur inflationary pressures, and he gave three possible reasons for the increases: Faster than expected economic growth, a greater than expected number of holidaymakers during Holy Week, or normal variations that would gradually correct themselves.
The latter two possible reasons should be discarded if the trend continues much longer, he said.

Other economists shared Cervera's view that the monetary base had exceeded the central bank's daily forecasts, but one said the amount -- around three billion pesos at most to levels around 80 billion pesos -- was not alarming.
J.P. Morgan economist Alfredo Thorne, meanwhile, said in a report on Monday that Mexican monetary policy was already tight after the latest rise in benchmark Treasury bill rates.
"Indeed, as gauged by J.P. Morgan's indicators and real interest rates, monetary conditions have persistently tightened in 1997," the report said.
